characters.name: Bob Oblong
characters.description: Born without arms or legs and works at a poison factory owned byGlobocide. Despite his deformities he is very chipper and sunny, and is modeled after various fathers from 1950s TV shows. Bumbling Dad: His naive nature keeps him from actively standing up to the Hill people and helping his family deal with their ilk. Cloudcuckoolander: There are multiple instances where Bob seems to operate in his own little world divorced from reality. In the episode where it's revealed Helga's parents are missing, she mentioned the last time they sent her money it was blue and red. Pickles joked that they were probably in Candyland before Bob goes on to explain that Candyland uses a barter system so if Helga's parents actuallywerethere, they'd have sent Helga candy canes or gumdrops instead of paper money. All Pickles can do is pat Bob's head and say "My poor baby." Everyone Has Standards: When reading Miss Hubbard's parenting advice book in "Milo Interrupted", he is immediately taken aback when he realizes it includes a racist prayer. Gag Penis: Not outright confirmed, but it is implied that Bob more than compensates for his lack of appendages with the one he has left; evidenced by Pickles' lust for him and the reactions of people watching him play the piano...

characters.name: Pickles Oblong
characters.description: A chain smoking alcoholic who was originally a Hill resident but moved to the valley after marrying Bob. All her hair has since fallen out due to the hazardous atmosphere of The Valley, and she is now regarded as an outcast by her former Hill friends. While not bitter about losing her privileged life, she often expresses disdain towards her self-centered former neighbors in the Hills. Action Mom: In "Heroine Addict", she risks her life to save her daughter Beth. The Alcoholic: Probably one of her most notable qualities. She rarely is without a drink in hand (it's even how she knows she's righthanded), once made homemade vermouth that was so potent that she needed medical treatment, and Bob refers to theDTs (a symptom of alcohol withdrawal also known as "the shakes") as a "mommy illness." Baldness Means Sickness: She lost her hair due to the exposure to the pollution of the Valley. Beehive Hairdo: Well wig, but it does resemble a tall beehive. A flashback episode even reveals she had very tall hair as a teenager, resembling one of the Debbies.

characters.name: Biff and Chip Oblong
characters.description: 17-year-old conjoined twins who are attached at the waist and share a middle leg. Biff is a hard worker obsessed with sports, while Chip is more laid back. Biff and Chip each occasionally go into "trances" to give the other brother privacy. Ambiguously Bi: It is frequently implied that Biff is gay and attracted to their coach (in fact, a DVD-exclusive special about how the show was created stated that Biff was gay and Chip was straight). However, Biff has occasionally been shown joining Chip in lusting over women. Big Brother Bully: On occasion, they pick on Milo. Conjoined Twins: They are joined at the waist and share a middle leg. Jerk Jock: While Biff is obsessed with sports, he can also be selfish i.e. destroying the house for fun, calling Milo an asshead and arguing with Chip all the time.

characters.name: Milo Oblong
characters.description: The youngest son and the series' protagonist. Often referred to by other kids as a "psycho", he is afflicted with numerous mental and social disorders and is on "everything from Ritalin to Rogaine." Despite his afflictions, he is a very forthright and benevolent boy, though he envies the Hill lifestyle and wishes to rise above his economic status. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: When he claims to have recovered from his mental disorders while at the dinner table, his father asks if that includes his Attention Deficit Disorderonly to see his son now playing with a butterfly outside. Charlie Brown Baldness: He only has one strand of hair, whether it's just how short hair is drawn on him or if he only has one hair due to a medical condition is unknown. Keet: He's loud, hyperactive, and kind of adorable. Loser Protagonist: Many of the episodes focus on him and you can't sink any lower if you live in a place as crappy as the valley part of Hill Valley.

characters.name: Beth Oblong
characters.description: The youngest child and only daughter, and has a warty, elongated growth growing out of her head. Despite her appendage, she appears to be significantly better adjusted than the rest of her family. Affectionate Nickname: Pickles calls her "sugar". Black Bead Eyes: Her eyes are black dots. Companion Cube: Slowie, which is apparently a bondage whip made to look like a doll. Deliberately Cute Child: She often uses her cuteness so she can get her way.

characters.name: Lucky
characters.description: The one-lungednoteHecoughed the other one up in the first episode, which Pickles mistook for a furballfamily cat who chain-smokes cigarettes and wears an uninterested, deadpan expression. Body Horror: He coughs up a lung in the pilot episode. Meaningful Name: He's "lucky" in the sense of "lucky to be alive", especially since he smokes and has one lung. The Stoic: Most of the time he has a deadpan expression.Not So Stoic: He was noticeably horrified by all those female cats in heat coming after him in "Father of the Bribe." Not So Stoic: He was noticeably horrified by all those female cats in heat coming after him in "Father of the Bribe."

characters.name: Scottie
characters.description: Milo's narcoleptic dog, a result of perfume used on him during his tenure as a test animal at Globocide. A Dog Named "Dog": He's a Scottish terrier named "Scottie" Canine Companion: He is Milo's pet. Nobody Poops: As the Klimers found out, he'll go when he needs to (averting this trope, but we don't see him poop on-screen) and this ends him up with being a test subject. Sleepyhead: Scottie was sprayed with a perfume that causes narcolepsy (but no longer causes night blindness or anal leakage).

characters.name: Helga Phugly
characters.description: A fat, toad-like girl who will eat virtually anything. She lives in a fantasy world, believing that she is pretty and popular and that the "Debbies" actually like her (believing this so stubbornly that when told that the Debbies hate her, she covered her ears, shut her eyes, and started stomping around humming very loudly). Adaptational Dumbass: InCreepy Susie and 13 Other Tragic Tales for Troubled Children, the book she was adapted from, she was very much aware that the Debbies didn't like her, as they regularly bullied her. She got her revenge by disguising herself as one of them, infiltrating their friend group, studying their habits and routines, before finally killing them during a sleepover. In the show, she has very little self-awareness, thinking she's more attractive and popular than she actually is, and is prone to stupid, self-destructive behavior in search of food. Animal Motifs: As said before, she looks like a toad, with a croaky voice to match. She also uses her tongue to catch her prey. Big Eater: She's pretty much obsessed with food. This turns out to be aJustified Tropewhen remembering she's been living without parents for so long she had no one to take care of her, so finding food became rather difficult. Black Speech: When she infers that Milo is telling others their secrets, Helga momentarily lapses into this, scaring the hell out of Peggy.

characters.name: Creepy Susie
characters.description: A girl who speaks with a deadpan French accent and appears to float instead of walk, as her legs are never shown. She is obsessed with death, and has a problem with pyromania, but it has been revealed she does enjoy hula hoops (even though her stiff movements make it physically impossible for her to use one). Adaptational Nice Guy: In the original book she and many of the other characters were adapted from, she's a loner with disturbing hobbies like collecting dead animals, and she killed a boy who had a crush on her simply because she didn't know how to handle her feelings. In the show, she can be morose and morbid, but is otherwise a decent person who actually has friends and has never hurt anyone. Creepy Good: She's a good person, but also has a macabre air- and isn't afraid to use it to her advantage. Dark Is Not Evil: While sinister, she's just as good-natured as the rest of the Valley people. Demoted to Extra: Believe it or not, a lot of the cast debuted in a book titledCreepy Susie and 13 Other Tragic Tales for Troubled Children. Mind you, she's only significant on the title and cover as it's an Anthology, but it's still kind of fascinating that it's her specifically and not the Oblong children.

characters.name: Peggy Weggy
characters.description: A one-breasted girl who lacks a lower jaw, causing her to spit and talk with a lisp. Despite her deformities, Peggy is incredibly cheerful and upbeat. Happily Adopted: By her fathers. No Mouth: Well, no lower jaw, none that is visible, anyway. Plucky Girl: She is always certain that things will turn out better for the Valley people eventually. Rhyming Names: Her full name is PeggyWeggy.

characters.name: Mikey Butts
characters.description: A boy saddled with a dangling, doubled posterior. Standard underwear will not fit him, so he wears his grandmother's old bra like backwards suspenders. He is also known to habitually probe his nose and ears with his finger. Butt-Monkey: No pun intended. More than any other character in the show, he frequently suffers misfortunes and gets injured. Depending on the Artist: Does Mikey have two butt cheeks, or three? Joke of the Butt: The deformity this Valley resident suffers is that he has a big, saggy behind. The Generic Guy: Doesn't really get a lot of characterization besides the, as he put it, "Ass Jokes" and picking his nose or ears.

characters.name: George Klimer
characters.description: Bob's rich and snobby boss. He represents the power and arrogance of the people of the Hills. He is very condescending to his employees, especially Bob and James. Bad Boss: The working conditions for his employees leave quite a lot to be desired. Corrupt Corporate Executive: He runs a poison company called Globocide and is a very contemptible bastard. You can't get any more corrupt than that. Eyes Always Shut: His eyes are always closed, but sometimes opened. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: For all his comic sociopathy and disdain for the Valley people, he seems to genuinely care about his daughter Debby (whichever one is his) in 'Disfigured Debby' he doesn't seem to care that she has lost her beauty, only that she hasn't been the same since being disfigured. Despite her face still being hideous and his obvious disdain for the Oblongs, he reacts with joy upon seeing that she's smiling for the first time since the accident, and is willing to forgo his pride to help her adjust to her new life.

characters.name: Pristine Klimer
characters.description: The wife of George and mother to Jared and Debbie. Pristine was good friends with Pickles before she married Bob, but abandoned her once she went to live in the valley. Ironic Name: "Pristine" means unspoiled and uncorrupted, which is ironic considering how she's vile and mean like the other Hill people. Politically Incorrect Villain: She looks down on the Valley people for their deformities and being lower-class like other Hill residents do, but she is also shown at one point talking down to a maid with pseudo-Spanish phrases even though the woman isn't even Hispanic.Pristine: Consuela, how do you say "You are not cleaning mi casa es bueno enough?" There isel spotto on el flooro.Maid: Mrs. Klimer. My name isKathy. I'm fromOhio. Rich Bitch: She's incredibly well off and wastes no time in insulting the Valley people. Socialite: She is married to one of the wealthiest people in Hill Valley and doesn't seem to have a job.

characters.name: Jared Klimer
characters.description: The arrogant son of George and Pristine and brother to one of the Debbies. He likes to taunt The Clubhouse Kids, along with his equally snobbish best friend Blaine. Ambiguously Gay: He is frequently seen with Blaine at his side and according to Milo there are rumors that they have sex with each other, although there are no implications about it beyond that. The Bully: He always picks on Milo. Malicious Misnaming: He's fond of calling Milo Oblong "Obdong".

characters.name: The Debbies
characters.description: A popular clique of identical girls who dress alike, much like theHeathersor the also-animated Ashleys fromRecess. The Debbies are often cruel to the valley kids, especially Helga who aspires to be accepted by them. Alpha Bitch: They are said to be the most popular girls in school while also taking every opportunity to pick on the Valley kids. A Day in the Limelight: In "Disfigured Debbie", Debbie Klimer is the victim of a thresher accident that makes her look hideously deformed, even after plastic surgery. The Valley people adopt her until she can get the surgery needed to make her look identical to the other Debbies again. Adaptational Nice Guy:Downplayed.InCreepy Susie And 13 Other Tragic Tales For Troubled Children, the Debbies chase Helga in their Jeep, brandishing a net. While the Debbies of the cartoon are arrogant and cold, they aren't sadistic like their book counterparts. Beehive Hairdo: They all sport a variant of this hairdo (think the hairstyle fromHairspray). The only exception to this isYvettewho had a slick pulled-back ponytail.

characters.name: Mayor Johnny "The Mayor" Bledsoe
characters.description: The town's mayor and a masked pro wrestler, a parody of pro wrestler-turned-elected officialJesse Ventura. He is corrupt, very bad at his job, and his daughter is a Debbie. Balls of Steel: Subverted when he orders Mr. Klimer tohit him in the crotch with a golf club. Sure, he looks fine, but his next line states otherwise: "That hurts more than I thought it would." Cool Mask: He always wears a luchador mask. Major Injury Underreaction: His response to getting hit in the groin after daring George Klimer to do so is to calmly remark that the experience is more painful than he expected it to be. Mayor Pain: Of both the incompetent and corrupt flavors. He's clearly not fit to run the town and is just as unpleasant as the other Hill people.

characters.name: Anita Bidet
characters.description: The owner of the bar Pickles frequents, The Rusty Bucket. Her name is a play on the phrase "I need a bidet." It is implied that she is a pre-op transgender woman, and though it is made obvious to viewers, none of the characters in the show seem to realize it. Beehive Hairdo: Her hive is a very elaborately curled red one. Fake Boobs: Her brassiere contains two large citrus fruit to fill 'em out, which are revealed when Pickles misfires a spear gun and pins them to a nearby tree (see here) Punny Name: A play on "I need a bidet". Trans Nature: She's a pre-op trans woman. The money she earns from owning/working The Rusty Bucket (most of which comes from Pickles, thanks to her alcoholism) goes towards her gender confirmation operation (which isn't outright stated, but even the most naive viewer can figure it out).Pickles: Hey, Anita, do you have a brother?Anita:Sure, why not?

characters.name: James
characters.description: Bob's hunchbacked co-worker. He is a people-pleaser and lacks self-esteem, buying friends on eBay to attend his bachelor party. Extreme Doormat: He pretty much sucks up to everyone because of how lonely he is.James:I'll take it!Peggy:But we didn't tell you what we're selling.noteFor context, they were sellingGirl Scoutcookies.James:I don't care, I'm a pleaser! Nice Guy: About as nice as anyone else in the Valley. No Celebrities Were Harmed: He sounds likePaul Lynde, though with a softer and higher pitch.

characters.name: Miss Hubbard
characters.description: An obnoxious,Holier than Thouspinster who's briefly named "Czar of Child Services" in the Valley. Abusive Parents: As a foster mother to Helga. She says she wanted to adopt Helga thinking she needed a loving home to raise her self esteem... then bombastically says the following:Miss. Hubbard: Lord, cleanse this vile heathen of her wicked, disgusting ways!Helga:I really don't like where this is going. Evil Old Folks: Possibly the oldest character in the show besides Granny Oblong, and likely the most vile. Alongside being an abusive caregiver and a dangerous gun fanatic, she's also shown to be rather racist when mentioning her own chastity belt. Pickles bluntly asks if Hubbard honestly thinks she needs it, to which Hubbard refers to "A lot of immigrants out there." Gun Nut: Carries around a hollowed-out bible concealing a loaded gun and practices taking apart and reassembling assault rifles before going to bed. In fact, when Bob calls on her for help to locate Miloafter Helga kidnapped him, the moment she got to the Oblong house sheburst into Milo's room and shot up his bed. Had Milo been in there at the time she would've killed him. Hate Sink: She's a bigoted, violent, domineering, judgmental shrew. EvenBobfinally admits she's a crazy old biddy.
